proposals.before: Book of Sui, 74th year of Volume, 39th year of Biography
proposals.after: Book of Sui, Volume 74, Biography 39
proposals.reason: The Chinese is a volume and biography heading (卷七十四列傳第三十九), not regnal or biographical 'years'.

proposals.before: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu and rose to the post of Defender-in-Chief.
proposals.after: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the post of General Who Leads the Army.
proposals.reason: 領軍將軍 is a palace-guard generalship, not 太尉 'Defender-in-Chief'. The literal line already has Commandery in the princely title.

proposals.before: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the office of Defender-in-Chief.
proposals.after: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the office of General Who Leads the Army.
proposals.reason: Same office error: 領軍將軍 is not Defender-in-Chief.

proposals.before: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shiwen was further promoted to Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo, and soon appointed Governor of Beizhou.
proposals.after: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shiwen was further granted Superior Kaifu rank, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo, and soon appointed Governor of Beizhou.
proposals.reason: 加上開府 adds the kaifu honor; 上柱國 'Superlative Pillar of State' is a different title not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo County, and soon after appointed Governor of Beizhou.
proposals.after: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was further given the rank of Superior Kaifu, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo County, and soon after appointed Governor of Beizhou.
proposals.reason: 加上開府 is additional kaifu status, not Superlative Pillar of State.

proposals.before: His father's younger sister's daughter had been a concubine of Qi and was beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue, as a concubine.
proposals.after: His paternal cousin (daughter of his father's brother) had been a concubine of Qi and was beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue, as a concubine.
proposals.reason: 從父妹 is a female cousin through the father's brother, not the daughter of a father's younger sister.

proposals.before: Under Emperor Ming of Zhou, at eighteen he was appointed Colonel and commanded local militia.
proposals.after: Under Emperor Ming of Zhou, at eighteen he was appointed Commander and commanded local militia.
proposals.reason: 都督 is a regional military commander (dudu), not the Western rank Colonel.

proposals.before: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou, at age eighteen he was appointed Colonel and commanded district troops.
proposals.after: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou, at age eighteen he was appointed Commander and commanded district troops.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 都督 as Colonel in the literal line.

proposals.before: Emperor Wu heard of this with approval, promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xindu, and appointed him Governor of Yanzhou.
proposals.after: Emperor Wu heard of this with approval, promoted him to Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xindu, and appointed him Governor of Yanzhou.
proposals.reason: 儀同三司 is not 開府儀同三司; Splendid Happiness with independent establishment overtranslates the office.

proposals.before: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for his merit was made Superlative Pillar of State, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liangquan.
proposals.after: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for his merit was made Superior Office-Opener, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liangquan.
proposals.reason: 上開府 is Superior Kaifu, not Superlative Pillar of State (上柱國).

proposals.before: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, for merit he was given Superlative Pillar of State, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.
proposals.after: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, for merit he was given Superior Office-Opener, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 上開府 as Superlative Pillar of State.

proposals.before: When Gaozu assumed overall command, Wei Chong rebelled at Yecheng and Shi followed Wei Xiaokuan to attack him.
proposals.after: When Gaozu assumed overall command, Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Yecheng and Shi followed Wei Xiaokuan to attack him.
proposals.reason: 尉迥 is Yuchi Jiong (尉遲迥); Wei Chong misreads both the surname and 迥.

proposals.before: When Gaozu assumed overall command, Wei Chong rose in rebellion at Yecheng; he followed Wei Xiaokuan to strike him.
proposals.after: When Gaozu assumed overall command, Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion at Yecheng; he followed Wei Xiaokuan to strike him.
proposals.reason: Same misidentification of 尉迥 as Wei Chong.

proposals.before: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was made General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou and devoted himself solely to imposing his authority.
proposals.after: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was made Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou and devoted himself solely to imposing his authority.
proposals.reason: 總管 is area commander-in-chief, not 大將軍 General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: Upon receiving the abdication he was appointed General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou, devoting himself solely to establishing authority.
proposals.after: Upon receiving the abdication he was appointed Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou, devoting himself solely to establishing authority.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 總管.

proposals.before: His son Xin, then a court grandee, came weeping and said, "Father, you are a veteran minister of the court and have committed no grave offense.
proposals.after: His son Xin, then a Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, came weeping and said, "Father, you are a veteran minister of the court and have committed no grave offense.
proposals.reason: 儀同 abbreviates 儀同三司, not a vague court grandee.

proposals.before: His son Xin was then a Grand Master for Court Audience; he came before Shi weeping and said: "Father, you are both an old minister of the court and have committed no great fault.
proposals.after: His son Xin was then a Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; he came before Shi weeping and said: "Father, you are both an old minister of the court and have committed no great fault.
proposals.reason: Grand Master for Court Audience does not render 儀同.

proposals.before: Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
proposals.reason: 廣州總管 is area commander-in-chief, not General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 總管 in the literal line.

proposals.before: He served under the Prince of Hejian in the attack on the Turks, and for merit was made Pillar of State and transferred to General-in-Chief of Qingzhou.
proposals.after: He served under the Prince of Hejian, Hong, in the attack on the Turks, and for merit was made Pillar of State and transferred to General-in-Chief of Qingzhou.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names the prince as 河間王弘; the idiomatic English drops the personal name 弘, which the literal line preserves as Hong.

proposals.before: At that time Yuan Hongsi was removed and appointed Chief Administrator of Youzhou; he feared being humiliated by Rong and firmly declined.
proposals.after: At that time Yuan Hongsi was appointed Chief Administrator of Youzhou; he feared being humiliated by Rong and firmly declined.
proposals.reason: 除為 here is the standard appointment formula, not removal from office; the idiomatic English already renders it as appointment only.

proposals.before: For merit he was appointed Great Colonel and soon managed palace guard duty.
proposals.after: For merit he was appointed Grand Commander and soon managed palace guard duty.
proposals.reason: 大都督 is a high military command rank (Grand Commander / Commander-in-chief), not 'Great Colonel'.

proposals.before: In the pacification of Qi he was promoted to Senior Grand Master for Court Audience and concurrently made Magistrate of Zhao Commandery.
proposals.after: In the pacification of Qi he was promoted to Senior Grand Master for Court Audience and concurrently made Grand Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
proposals.reason: 太守 of a 郡 is a commandery grand administrator/governor, not a magistrate.

proposals.before: When Wang Qian rebelled, Zhongqing was in Lizhou and at once joined General-in-Chief Dou Lu Ji in raising troops to resist.
proposals.after: When Wang Qian rebelled, Zhongqing was in Lizhou and at once joined Area Commander Dou Lu Ji in raising troops to resist.
proposals.reason: 總管 here is an area command (Area Commander-in-chief), not the separate rank 'General-in-Chief' (大將軍).

proposals.before: In the third year of Kaihuang, when the Turks raided the frontier, he served as Campaign Commander under the Prince of Hejian to Helan Mountain.
proposals.after: In the third year of Kaihuang, when the Turks raided the frontier, he served as Campaign Commander under Hong, Prince of Hejian, to Helan Mountain.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names the prince 弘; the idiomatic English drops the personal name present in the source and the literal rendering.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Governor of Yanzhou but, before taking office, was appointed General-in-Chief of Shuozhou.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Governor of Yanzhou but, before taking office, was appointed Area Commander-in-chief of Shuozhou.
proposals.reason: 朔州總管 is the Shuozhou area command, not General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: The court feared Tardu would strike Qimin by surprise and ordered Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops in reserve; Han Hong, Acting General-in-Chief of Daizhou, Li Yaowang, Duke of Yongkang, Liu Long, Governor of Wei, and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.
proposals.after: The court feared Tardu would strike Qimin by surprise and ordered Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops in reserve; Han Hong, Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou, Li Yaowang, Duke of Yongkang, Liu Long, Governor of Wei Prefecture, and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.
proposals.reason: 代州總管 is Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou, not Acting General-in-Chief; 蔚州 is Wei Prefecture, easily confused with 魏.

proposals.before: The court feared Tardu would launch a surprise attack on Qimin and ordered Zhongqing to garrison twenty thousand troops in readiness; Acting General-in-Chief of Daizhou Han Hong, Duke of Yongkang Li Yaowang, and Governor of Wei Zhou Liu Long and others led ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Heng'an.
proposals.after: The court feared Tardu would launch a surprise attack on Qimin and ordered Zhongqing to garrison twenty thousand troops in readiness; Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou Han Hong, Duke of Yongkang Li Yaowang, and Governor of Wei Prefecture Liu Long and others led ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Heng'an.
proposals.reason: Literal English invents 'Wei Zhou' from 蔚州 and misrenders 總管 as Acting General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: When the Prince of Shu Xiu fell from grace he was ordered to Yizhou to investigate exhaustively.
proposals.after: When Xiu, Prince of Shu, fell from grace he was ordered to Yizhou to investigate exhaustively.
proposals.reason: 蜀王秀 is the Prince of Shu, named Xiu; 'Prince of Shu Xiu' fuses title and given name.

proposals.before: After Emperor Wu conquered Qi he was promoted to Superlative Pillar of State and Duke of Ye, granted three thousand lengths of goods, three thousand shi of grain, a hundred slaves, and thousands of livestock.
proposals.after: Following Emperor Wu in destroying Qi he was promoted to Superlative Opening Office and Duke of Ye County, granted three thousand lengths of goods, three thousand shi of grain, a hundred slaves, and thousands of livestock.
proposals.reason: Chinese 上開府 is the honorific office Shang Kaifu, not 上柱國 (Pillar of State); 鄴縣公 is specifically Duke of Ye County; 從 marks accompaniment in the campaign.

proposals.before: Xin sent Hongdu to admonish him with warnings of fortune and ruin; Chen withdrew by evening.
proposals.after: Xin sent Hongdu to admonish him with warnings of fortune and ruin; Pan Chen withdrew by evening.
proposals.reason: 琛 here is Pan Chen's given name, not the Chen polity; the idiomatic 'Chen' collapses the person into the dynasty name.

proposals.before: When Wei Chong rebelled, Hongdu served as Campaign Commander under Wei Xiaokuan.
proposals.after: When Wei Jiong rebelled, Hongdu served as Campaign Commander under Wei Xiaokuan.
proposals.reason: 迥 is Jiong, not Chong; the English personal name mistranscribes the given name.

proposals.before: He was soon transferred to General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
proposals.after: He was soon transferred to Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
proposals.reason: 總管 is regional commander-in-chief (zongguan), not the office usually rendered General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: When the Liang prince Xiao Cong came to court, the emperor appointed Hongdu General-in-Chief of Jiangling to garrison Jingzhou.
proposals.after: When the Liang prince Xiao Cong came to court, the emperor appointed Hongdu Area Commander-in-Chief of Jiangling to garrison Jingzhou.
proposals.reason: 江陵總管 is Jiangling area commander-in-chief, not General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: When Wei Chong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
proposals.after: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
proposals.reason: 尉迥 names the Xiangzhou rebel Yuchi Jiong (尉遲迥), not a person named Wei Chong.

proposals.before: When Wei Chong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
proposals.after: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
proposals.reason: The literal field repeats the same misidentification of 尉迥 as Wei Chong.

proposals.before: Soon he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
proposals.after: Soon he was further given the rank of Senior Commander Unequaled in Honor, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
proposals.reason: 上開府 is Shang Kaifu, not Superlative Pillar of State (上柱國).

proposals.before: Soon he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
proposals.after: Soon he was further given the rank of Senior Commander Unequaled in Honor, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
proposals.reason: The literal field likewise renders 上開府 as Superlative Pillar of State.

proposals.before: Yet Hongdu managed his household like an office; his sons and younger brothers, though gray-haired, were beaten and flogged when they moved; the inner gates were stern and orderly, and he was praised by his contemporaries.
proposals.after: Yet Hongdu managed his household like an office; his sons and younger brothers, though gray-haired, were beaten and flogged at the slightest move; the inner gates were stern and orderly, and he was praised by his contemporaries.
proposals.reason: 動行捶楚 means they were flogged for any action, not that beating occurred when they moved house.

proposals.before: Later, because of his status as an imperial relative, his treatment grew still more generous and he was made General-in-Chief of Xiang Prefecture.
proposals.after: Later, because of his status as an imperial relative, his treatment grew still more generous and he was made Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiang Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 襄州總管 is an area command, not the title General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: During Kaihuang he was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience for military merit, then Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
proposals.after: During Kaihuang he was appointed Equal-in-Rites (Yitong) for military merit, then Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
proposals.reason: 儀同 is the honorific rank Yitong (儀同三司), not Grand Master for Court Audience (朝請大夫).

proposals.before: In Kaihuang for military merit he was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience; soon he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
proposals.after: In Kaihuang for military merit he was appointed Equal-in-Rites (Yitong); soon he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
proposals.reason: 儀同 is Yitong, not Grand Master for Court Audience.

proposals.before: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Household; for offending the throne he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan.
proposals.after: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; for offending the throne he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan.
proposals.reason: 光祿少卿 is vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Imperial Household.

proposals.before: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Household; for offending the emperor's intent he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan Commandery.
proposals.after: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; for offending the emperor's intent he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan Commandery.
proposals.reason: 光祿少卿 is vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

proposals.before: For those who follow, in taking up office and public life: even if one cannot rise like Zi Gao with honor waiting at one's gate, must one reduce one's mother to sweeping the grave and watching for the funeral train?
proposals.after: For those who follow, in taking up office and public life: even if one cannot raise a high gate awaiting enfeoffment, must one reduce one's mother to sweeping the grave and watching for the funeral train?
proposals.reason: 子高門以待封 is the set phrase of a high gate awaiting enfeoffment, not a personal name Zi Gao.

proposals.before: Scholars who come after, in establishing themselves and engaging in government—even if they cannot be like Zi Gao with his gate awaiting enfeoffment—how can they allow their mothers to sweep graves while watching for funeral processions?
proposals.after: Scholars who come after, in establishing themselves and engaging in government—even if they cannot make a high gate awaiting enfeoffment—how can they allow their mothers to sweep graves while watching for funeral processions?
proposals.reason: Chinese 子高門 is high gate, not the person Zi Gao invented in the English.

decisions.reason: 卷七十四列傳第三十九 is a fascicle and biography heading, not regnal or biographical years; the replacement matches the Chinese.

decisions.after: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the office of General of the Palace Guard.

進位儀同三司 is Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, not 開府儀同三司 (Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment).

decisions.after: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for his merit was made Superior Kaifu, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liangquan.
decisions.reason: 加上開府 is Superior Kaifu, not 上柱國; 'Superior Office-Opener' is an awkward calque, so the established Kaifu rendering is used.

decisions.after: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, for merit he was given Superior Kaifu, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.
decisions.reason: The literal line has the same 上開府/上柱國 error; Superior Kaifu is the accurate office name.

拜襄州總管 is an area command (zongguan), not 大將軍 (General-in-Chief).
The literal line has the same 總管/General-in-Chief error.
時為儀同 abbreviates 儀同三司, a ranked honor, not a vague 'court grandee'.
Grand Master for Court Audience renders 朝請大夫, not 儀同.
廣州總管 is the Guangzhou area command, not General-in-Chief.
The literal line repeats the 總管 mistranslation.

decisions.after: He served under Hong, Prince of Hejian, in the attack on the Turks, and for merit was made Senior Pillar of State and transferred to Area Commander-in-Chief of Qingzhou.
decisions.reason: 河間王弘 names the prince 弘, which the original omits; the proposal still leaves 上柱國 as mere Pillar of State and 青州總管 as General-in-Chief.

decisions.reason: 被除為幽州長史 is the appointment formula 除為, not removal from office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元弘嗣被除為幽州長史

decisions.reason: 大都督 is a high command rank, not 'Great Colonel' (a rendering of 校尉-type titles).
趙郡太守 is the commandery administrator (taishou), not a county magistrate.
總管豆盧勣 identifies Doulu Ji by the area-command post 總管, not 大將軍.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與總管豆盧勣發兵拒守

decisions.reason: 從河間王弘 names the prince 弘; restoring Hong does not invent or distort the Chinese.
朔州總管 is the Shuozhou area command, not General-in-Chief.

decisions.after: The court feared Tardu would strike Qimin by surprise and ordered Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops in reserve; Han Hong, Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou, Li Yaowang, Duke of Yongkang, Liu Long, Governor of Yuzhou, and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.
decisions.reason: 代州總管 is not Acting General-in-Chief; 蔚州 is Yuzhou, and 'Wei Prefecture' still collides with 魏.

decisions.after: The court feared Tardu would launch a surprise attack on Qimin and ordered Zhongqing to garrison twenty thousand troops in readiness; Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou Han Hong, Duke of Yongkang Li Yaowang, and Governor of Yuzhou Liu Long and others led ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Heng'an.
decisions.reason: 'Governor of Wei Zhou' invents a place from 蔚州, and 總管 is not Acting General-in-Chief; Yuzhou is the prefecture named.
蜀王秀 is the Prince of Shu, named Xiu; 'the Prince of Shu Xiu' already names title and given name, so the proposed reordering is stylistic.

尉迥作亂相州 is Yuchi Jiong's rebellion at Xiangzhou, not a person named Wei Chong.

decisions.reason: 加上開府 is Superior Kaifu, not 上柱國; 'Senior Commander Unequaled in Honor' conflates 上開府 with 儀同三司.

decisions.after: Soon he was further given the rank of Superior Kaifu, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
decisions.reason: The literal line has the same 上開府 error; Senior Commander Unequaled in Honor is not that office.

decisions.after: In Kaihuang for military merit he was appointed Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; soon he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 縱不能為子高門以待封

decisions.after: Scholars who come after, in establishing themselves and engaging in government—even if they cannot make a high gate for their sons awaiting enfeoffment—how can they allow their mothers to sweep graves while watching for funeral processions?
decisions.reason: 子高門 is not the person Zi Gao; the replacement still omits 為子 (for one's sons).

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Wei Chong was produced by misreading 尉迥; the source names Yuchi Jiong.
